the eIF3e subunit of the translation initiation factor 3 (eIF3) is required for inducer-dependent eIF4E Ser-209 phosphorylation and that eIF3 is required for the recruitment of 40S ribosomes to the 5′ end of the mRNA.

the regulation of gene expression by post-transcriptional mechanisms.
the molecular mechanisms by which cells regulate the translation of mRNA and the consequences of this regulation on the development of cancer.
the molecular mechanisms of eukaryotic protein synthesis, particularly the role of eukaryoticeukaryotic translation factor 3 (eIF3) in translation initiation.

the eIF3e protein is required for inducer-dependent eIF4E modification and that eIF3 is required to coordinate the recruitment of 40S subunits to the mRNA 3′ end with the modification of a cap binding initiation factor.
this study establishes a mechanism of translational control by 40S ribosomes that is dependent on eIF3e.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we identified an eIF3 component that regulates eIF3 function.
eIF3 is required for the phosphorylation of the cap binding protein eIF4E, which in turn is required for 40S ribosomal subunit recruitment to mRNA.
eIF3 is required for the phosphorylation of eIF4E, which in turn is required for the recruitment of the 40S ribosomal subunit.
The main takeaway from our work is that
eIF4E and eIF3e form a functional module that is required for translation initiation and selective mRNA translation.
the 40S ribosomal subunit, through eIF3, can influence translation initiation by regulating the phosphorylation state of the eIF4F cap-binding complex.
eIF3 subunits can function in multiple roles during translation initiation.
